paragraphs: Swamiji described the world as a huge gymnasium. You, I and millions of others come here to work out and become strong and perfect. That is its purpose. It isn't that God couldn't have made a perfect universe or couldn't remove its pain.

Then he reminded his audience of a funny story. A clergyman and a young lady were both peering at the moon through a telescope and noticed dark spots on it. The clergyman was certain they were the spires of churches. The young lady scoffed: obviously they were young lovers kissing!
We do the same thing with the world, said Swamiji. We see it from wherever we happen to stand, and we think that view shows us the whole truth. What we see depends on the level we are living on.

Take the fire in your kitchen. In itself it is neither good nor bad. When it cooks your dinner, you praise it. When it burns your finger, you call it a nuisance. It would be just as accurate, he said, to say that the universe itself is neither good nor evil. The world is simply the world, and it will always be so.
learn: We often judge things by how they affect us right now, and then call that the truth. Remember the telescope: what you see says as much about you as about the world. Treat life's ups and downs as workouts that make you stronger.
